newsitem.title: GREECE: British embassy issues travel warning on Greece.
newsitem.headline: British embassy issues travel warning on Greece.

text.p: Britain has warned visitors to Greece that a transport backlog from a seamen's strike and the renewed threat of a road blockade by farmers could disrupt their travel plans, the British Consulate in Athens said on Friday.
"It's not telling people not to come. It's making them aware of problems and advising them to check the situation before they arrive," British Consul Gordon Bernard told Reuters.
Greece is sensitive to travel advisories by foreign governments because tourism is one of its top foreign exchange earners.

"Although the seamen's strike is now over, congestion due to timetable problems is likely to continue for a few days," the advisory said. "Greek farmers are also threatening to blockade road and rail links."
It said visitors should modify their plans and drivers should check the local situation before they begin their trips.
A crippling 10-day strike by seamen, which ended on Thursday, left passengers and trucks stranded at ports around Greece and cut off remote Aegean islands.

Farmers, who stopped cross-country traffic for 25 days in November and December, are threatening to block highways and rail lines with tractors again if demands for cheaper fuel, lower taxes and higher price supports are not met by February 4.
